title: Secondary and bridge heating guide the redesign

takeaway.text: Secondary and input-bridge heating motivate lower winding and rectifier losses and wider current and heat paths.

visible_content.condition: V2 · Electronic load at secondary output
visible_content.equilibrium_caption: No load point reached thermal equilibrium
visible_content.design_response: Design direction: reduce winding and rectifier loss; widen bridge current and heat paths

speaker_notes:
The images show the 70.75-watt and final 137.08-watt points in the same direct secondary-load sequence. R3 covers the input bridge and R1 the secondary area. These are maximum surface readings within each region, not junction temperatures. The input bridge peaked at 83.9 degrees Celsius at the intermediate point and then varied at the higher loads. The secondary region rose to 98.3 degrees at the final point, showing substantial heating in the secondary area.

The bridge diodes were replaced, but the heating remained. Limited copper and a possible restriction through a single interlayer via could contribute. Wider bridge copper and via paths would improve current distribution and heat spreading. On the secondary side, the observed heating motivates reducing winding and rectifier losses and improving their current paths. These are proposed design changes.
transition: Together, these results define the contribution and the present limit of the supply.

sources.supports: Heating persisted after diode replacement; limited copper and a possible single-via connection were suspected, not confirmed.

facts: All seven paired region maxima and rounded secondary powers match the V2 summary; R3 peaks at point 2, 83.9 °C and 70.75 W; R1 reaches 98.3 °C at point 7, 137.08 W.
R3 and R1 are regional surface maxima, not junction temperatures; the camera scale tops at 85.1 °C although the R1 readout is 98.3 °C. The original scale and readout are retained.
No load point reached equilibrium; the footer states this once, and the chart joins successive readings only.

Bridge diode replacement did not resolve the heating. A copper or via restriction is a suspected cause, while the proposed winding, rectifier and current-path changes are engineering directions rather than completed changes.
All original camera labels and the unchanged chart data are retained; the design_response and phase_label are added for the current layout.

The lower-power photo is the unchanged Capture 017 image, paired by timestamp to secondary power 70.751393856 W; R3 is 83.9 °C and R1 is 57.2 °C. Input power and efficiency for this capture are not used.
